text: Index health, integrity checks, and backup verification have all depended on someone remembering to do them by hand. This lesson automates that memory away.

A dedicated Automation Account, thornridge-automation, runs three PowerShell runbooks on fixed schedules: fragmentation-driven index maintenance weekly, a DBCC CHECKDB integrity check nightly, and a real backup-restore verification monthly.
The index runbook queries actual fragmentation stats and only rebuilds or reorganizes what needs it, authenticating with a managed identity instead of a stored password.

The backup-verification runbook is the one most teams skip: it actually restores a point-in-time backup to a throwaway database, checks it has real data, then tears it down -- proving the recovery point is achievable, not assumed.
Routine maintenance now runs itself, with an alert on any failure. Next: putting the database's own schema under the same version control and review discipline as the application code.
